title: Prime Number Calculator
description: Check if a number is prime, see its full prime factorization, and find the nearest primes.

formula.summary: A number is prime if it has no divisors other than 1 and itself, checked here by trial division up to its square root.
formula.expression: n is prime if no integer d in [2, √n] divides n evenly

examples.title: Is 97 prime?
examples.note: Yes - 97 has no divisors between 2 and √97 ≈ 9.8

faqs.question: Why only check up to the square root?
faqs.answer: If n has a divisor larger than its square root, it must also have a corresponding divisor smaller than the square root, so checking beyond that point is always redundant.

faqs.question: Is 1 a prime number?
faqs.answer: No - by definition, prime numbers must have exactly two distinct positive divisors (1 and themselves). 1 has only one divisor, so it's excluded.

seoContent.heading: What makes a number prime
seoContent.body: A prime number is a whole number greater than 1 that can only be evenly divided by 1 and itself - 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, and 13 are the first few. Every other whole number greater than 1 (a 'composite' number) can be broken down into a unique product of prime numbers, known as its prime factorization.

seoContent.heading: Trial division: a simple but effective test
seoContent.body: The trial division method checks whether any number from 2 up to the square root of n divides evenly into n. This is efficient enough for numbers up into the millions and is the same basic principle used to teach primality testing in most math curricula.
